title: Karl Organizing: Physical Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Physical Training] A friend asked me: 'Do we need to learn how to fight for community defense?' What do I tell them?

It’s better to have the skills and not need them than to be helpless when a fascist or a rogue cop gets physical. Host basic self-defense or de-escalation classes in your backyard or a local gym. Focus on how to break grips, protect your head, and move as a unit. We don't look for fights, but we sure as hell know how to end them if they're forced on us.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Sharing] Can you explain: how do we handle money and tools between different groups?

Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else.

title: Karl Organizing: Power Mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Power Mapping] Can you explain: how do we know which politician or CEO to target first?

Look, Map out who actually signs the checks or passes the laws, then find out who those people are actually afraid of. Don't just protest into the void; find the specific person—the landlord, the CEO, the Council Chair—who has the power to give you what you want right now. Once you find that pressure point, you squeeze together as a coalition until they crack under the weight.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: inclusivity in Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: inclusivity in Action] Give me the short version: How do we make sure our coalition isn't just one type of person?

Go to where the people are instead of waiting for them to find your meeting in a basement. If you want immigrant workers in your coalition, you need translators and you need to show up for their fights before you ask them to show up for yours. Solidary isn't a feeling you get; it's a practice of showing up for people who the system tries to make invisible.

title: Karl Organizing: Signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signature Gathering] How do we get on the ballot without a massive paid staff?

Here's the thing: You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. Set up at grocery stores, transit hubs, and public parks to meet people where they already are. Treat every signature as a conversation and a potential new recruit for the movement, not just a box to check. We don't need consultants when we have a disciplined crew of comrades who know how to ask a neighbor for two minutes of their time.

title: Karl Organizing: Building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Building Trust] A friend asked me: 'How do we trust people we have never worked with before?' What do I tell them?

Trust is built through sweat and shared risk, not long meetings and promises. Start with a small, low-stakes action like a joint flyer drop or a community meal to see who actually shows up when it is raining. If they do the work, they are in; if they just want to talk in circles while you're trying to organize, keep them at arm's length. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Booking Process
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Booking Process] What's going to happen to me once I'm inside the precinct?

They'll take your prints, your photo, and your property, but they can't take your dignity. Keep your head up, don't answer any questions about the protest, and don't sign anything without a lawyer looking at it first. Every hour you spend in there is a testament to your commitment to the fight against these billionaires' pets. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, secure Document Sharing] How can I send sensitive files to my organizing committee safely?

Real talk: Stop using Google Drive or Dropbox; those companies are just extensions of the state surveillance machine. Use OnionShare or a password-protected, encrypted zip file sent through an end-to-end encrypted channel. If the document is truly dangerous, put it on a thumb drive and hand it over in person. Digital trails are permanent; physical hand-offs are much harder to intercept.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, accountability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, accountability] What if one group isn't doing the work they promised to do?

Have a direct, face-to-face conversation and ask them what the bottleneck is. If they are overwhelmed, offer help; if they are just being lazy or posturing, tell them they are holding back the whole movement. We don't have time for passengers when we're trying to sink the billionaire's ship, so everyone has to pull their weight or get out of the way.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital Organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital Organizing] Can you explain: how much time should we spend on social media versus knocking doors?

Here's how it works: Digital is for broadcasting the message and calling people to action, but the doors are where the actual votes are won. Use your online presence to document the campaign’s energy and show the bosses that we’re a growing force. Don't get trapped in pointless Twitter feuds with trolls who don't even live in your district. Use every post to drive people toward a physical meeting or a canvassing shift—online noise must lead to offline power.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, burner Devices] How do I get a burner phone without looking suspicious?

Don't go to the shop next to your house, and for the love of the movement, pay with cash. Buy a cheap flip phone and a prepaid SIM at a big box store where you're just another face in the crowd. Never turn it on at your house or link it to your personal accounts. A burner is for the mission, not for checking your personal emails. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: New Neighbor Outreach
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[New Neighbor Outreach] A new family just moved in. How do we bring them into the union?

Look, Don't wait for them to have a problem; go over with a housewarming gift and the union's contact info on day one. Explain that the building stays safe and the rent stays stable only because you all look out for each other. Getting them on board early prevents the landlord from using them as a 'scab' to undermine the collective power you've built.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: internal Conflict
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: internal Conflict] Give me the short version: What do we do when two groups in the coalition start fighting each other?

Drag them back to the shared demand and remind them who the real enemy is. If the beef is personal, tell them to settle it on their own time because the warehouse workers or the tenants are waiting on us to lead. We aren't here to be a family; we are here to be a fist, and a fist doesn't work if the fingers are trying to snap each other. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Union busting consultants
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Union busting consultants] My company hired a 'workplace consultant.' What does that mean?

Real talk: It means they're spending six figures to stop you from getting a raise. Those consultants charge $3,000 a day to scare workers with captive-audience meetings and legal threats. Everything they tell you is designed to make solidarity feel risky and obedience feel safe. The consultant leaves when the campaign ends; your coworkers are there every day. Organize anyway.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, sustainer Programs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, sustainer Programs] Is it better to ask for one big check or small monthly amounts?

Real talk: Give me ten comrades chipping in ten bucks a month over one guy writing a thousand-dollar check any day of the week. Monthly sustainers provide the predictable floor we need to plan long-term campaigns without panicking about the rent. It builds a base of people who are spiritually and financially committed to the long haul, not just a one-time thrill.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: grant Alternatives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: grant Alternatives] Give me the short version: Foundation grants seem easier than grassroots fundraising. Why avoid them?

Foundations are just tax shelters for the wealthy designed to domesticate the revolution. They'll bury you in paperwork and 'deliverables' until you're too busy writing reports to actually organize. We build our own solidarity funds through community dinners and sustainer circles so we never have to ask a board of directors for permission to speak the truth.

title: Karl Organizing: Post-Protest Care
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Post-Protest Care] I feel really shaken up after being arrested. Is that normal?

It’s completely normal, comrade; the state uses violence and cages to try and break your spirit. Get some food, get some sleep, and talk to a movement-aligned counselor or your affinity group about it. We need you healthy and ready for the long haul, so take the time to heal before you jump back to the front lines.

title: Karl Organizing: After the Win
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[After the Win] Can you explain: what happens to the coalition once we actually win our main demand?

Here's how it works: Don't you dare go home and think the job is done. Use the structure you built to find the next target, because the billionaires will be plotting to take back what you just won the second you stop looking. A coalition shouldn't just be for one crisis; it should be the foundation for a permanent power base that the ruling class can never dismantle.

title: Karl Organizing: Transportation Networks
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Transportation Networks] How can we help neighbors who don't have cars get to grocery stores or doctors?

Start a dispatch thread where comrades with vehicles can post their availability for the week. If you're going to the store anyway, check the list and see which neighbor needs a ride or a delivery. We can bypass the predatory ride-share apps by simply looking out for each other and pooling our gas money. It's about making sure no one is trapped in their home just because they can't afford a mechanic.

title: Karl Organizing: Diversity in organizing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Diversity in organizing] Our shop is very divided by race and language. How do we unite?

Your organizing committee must look like the workforce. If half the shop speaks Spanish, you need Spanish-speaking leaders. If you ignore one group, the boss will use that 'divide and conquer' strategy to pit you against each other. Find the common grievances that cut across every line—like respect and fair pay—and build a bridge of solidarity that the boss can't blow up.

title: Karl Organizing: Meeting Facilitation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Meeting Facilitation] How do we keep one person from dominating our organizing meetings?

Karl's answer: Use a progressive stack where you prioritize people who haven't spoken yet or are from marginalized groups. Set a firm time limit for each person and have a facilitator who isn't afraid to cut off a rambler. Good organizing requires everyone's voice, not just the one who speaks the loudest.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medic Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medic Support] A friend asked me: 'What should a basic street medic kit include for a local protest?' What do I tell them?

Pack plenty of saline for eye flushes, sterile gauze, medical tape, and a lot of nitrile gloves. Don't forget liquid antacid mixed with water for pepper spray, and keep some high-calorie snacks for folks who get lightheaded. Mark yourself clearly with a red cross or 'MEDIC' tape so people know where to run when the heat turns up. We look after our own because we know the police are only there to protect property, not people.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, rapid Response Setup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, rapid Response Setup] How do I start a network to stop raids in my area?

Grab five friends you trust and get on an encrypted app like Signal right now. Map out your blocks and assign roles—scouts to spot the vans, legal observers, and phone-tree captains. When a raid starts, you don't panic; you flood the street with bodies and cameras to make the state's dirty work impossible. It's about being faster and more organized than the guys in tactical vests.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: security Culture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: security Culture] Give me the short version: How do we keep our coalition safe from people trying to break us up?

Keep your sensitive planning to small, vetted groups and leave the public posturing for the rallies. Don't talk about illegal tactics on apps that the cops can read, and verify the identity of anyone who wants access to your data or money. Paranoia is a trap, but being smart about who knows what is just basic survival in a fight against people with infinite resources. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Conflict Resolution
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Conflict Resolution] Two people in our collective are fighting and it's stalling our work. What now?

Sit them down with a neutral mediator and remind them that our real enemy is the ruling class, not each other. Focus on the harm caused and how to make it right rather than looking for someone to blame or 'cancel.' If we can't solve problems within our own ranks, we'll never be able to build a world that works for everyone. Keep the focus on the mission: feeding and protecting our people. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Digital security basics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Digital security basics] How do I keep my phone safe at a protest?

Turn off biometric unlock — use a strong passcode. Disable location services. Use Signal, not SMS. Better yet: bring a burner or leave your main phone home. Cops use stingrays to vacuum up every phone in the area. Your phone is a tracking device that happens to make calls — treat it like one. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: safe Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: safe Zones] Give me the short version: How do we make our neighborhood a 'no-go' zone for ICE?

Look, Get local businesses to display stickers stating they won't let feds in without a warrant and train their staff on what to say. Map out every alley and 'safe house' where neighbors can duck in if they're being followed. Run regular drills so everyone knows exactly where to go when the alert hits. We create safety by making our neighborhoods too organized for the state to operate in.

title: Karl Organizing: Accountability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Accountability] Can you explain: what if one group isn't doing the work they promised to do?

Real talk: Have a direct, face-to-face conversation and ask them what the bottleneck is. If they are overwhelmed, offer help; if they are just being lazy or posturing, tell them they are holding back the whole movement. We don't have time for passengers when we're trying to sink the billionaire's ship, so everyone has to pull their weight or get out of the way.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, neighborhood Pods
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, neighborhood Pods] How many houses should be in one neighborhood pod to keep it manageable?

Real talk: Keep it tight—ten to fifteen households is the sweet spot for actually knowing your neighbors' names and needs. If it gets too big, communication breaks down and people start feeling like a number again. You want a group where one person can walk to everyone else's front door in five minutes if the internet goes down. Once you hit twenty houses, it's time to split and help the next block start their own pod.

title: Karl Organizing: Enemy Counter-Fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Enemy Counter-Fundraising] How do we use our opposition to raise money?

Here's the thing: Nothing opens wallets faster than a common enemy. When a billionaire or a corrupt politician attacks your movement, use their own words to show your supporters why we're winning. Frame every contribution as a direct middle finger to the people trying to silence us, and watch the resources pour in from people who are fed up.

title: Karl Organizing: Corporate Landlords
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Corporate Landlords] We rent from a massive corporation based in another state. How do we fight someone we can't see?

Here's how it works: Every corporation has a face and an address. Find out who the CEO is, where they live, and who their investors are. Don't just picket the local leasing office; take the fight to their corporate headquarters or the fancy gala they're attending. Use the internet to find other buildings they own and link up with those tenants to create a multi-city front that hits their stock price.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: kettling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: kettling] Give me the short version: What should we do if the police box us in from all sides?

Don't panic—that's exactly what they want. Keep the crowd calm, look for weak points in their line, and start filming immediately to document that they've trapped you without an exit. Kettling is a move used by cowards to manufacture a reason for mass arrests, so stay close to your comrades and keep your spirits high.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, building Trust
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, building Trust] How do I get my neighbors to trust me with their safety?

Stop talking and start doing. Help people with their groceries, clean up the local park, and show up when someone's car breaks down. Trust isn't built in a meeting; it's built in the daily work of being a good neighbor. People won't call you during a raid if they don't know you're someone who keeps their word. Solidarity is a practice, not a slogan.

title: Karl Organizing: Ethical Banking
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Ethical Banking] Where should we keep the movement's cash so it's safe?

Here's how it works: Get your money out of the big Wall Street banks that fund pipelines and private prisons yesterday. Move the war chest to a local credit union or a community-owned bank where the staff actually knows your name. It won't solve capitalism, but at least your deposits aren't being used as a weapon against your own comrades while you sleep.

title: Karl Organizing: Direct Action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct Action] The landlord is ignoring our letters. What's the next step?

If they won't hear you, make it so they can't ignore you. Take the union to the landlord's office, their church, or their favorite restaurant and pass out flyers to everyone they know. Disrupt their 'good reputation' in the community. When you make their private greed a public embarrassment, the cost of fixing your plumbing suddenly becomes cheaper than the cost of the bad publicity. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Account Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Account Security] Can you explain: what should I do if I think my account was hacked?

Assume the device is compromised. Use a different, clean device to change your master passwords and revoke all active sessions. Alert your comrades immediately so they don't fall for any phishing links sent from your account. If we don't look out for each other, the enemy wins. Once the breach is contained, wipe the infected device and start fresh. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Surveillance Awareness] A friend asked me: 'What is a Stingray and should I be worried about it?' What do I tell them?

A Stingray is a fake cell tower the feds use to hijack your phone's signal and track your location. They use them to map out who is at a protest and who they're talking to. Put your phone in a Faraday bag or turn on Airplane Mode when you're near the action. If you don't need to coordinate in real-time, leave the tracking device at home.

title: Karl Organizing: Right to Remain Silent
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Right to Remain Silent] What should I say if a cop starts questioning me at a rally?

You say absolutely nothing except 'I am exercising my right to remain silent' and 'I want a lawyer.' These pigs aren't looking for the truth; they're looking for a reason to put a comrade in a cage. Shut your mouth, stay firm, and don't let their friendly routine trick you into betraying the movement. Silence is your best weapon in the back of a squad car.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medics] What should I have in my bag if I want to be a street medic?

Karl's answer: Pack plenty of saline for eye flushes, sterile gauze, medical tape, and nitrile gloves. Carry a few doses of Narcan and know how to use them, along with plenty of water and snacks for low blood sugar. Your job is to keep people in the fight, so focus on quick patches and getting folks to safety. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Merch Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Merch Strategy] What kind of merch actually makes money for the movement?

Forget the cheap plastic trinkets that end up in a landfill. Print bold, defiant designs on union-made shirts or screen-print patches that comrades can sew onto their own gear to show their colors. Sell items that serve a purpose, like heavy-duty water bottles or thick canvas bags, and make sure every cent above cost goes toward organizing the next action.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, escalation Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, escalation Management] What if the police get aggressive while we are watching them?

Hold your ground but don't give them an easy excuse to start swinging or shooting. Keep your cameras high and clearly state that you are peacefully observing. If they move in, back up slowly as a group, keeping your eyes on them the whole time. The goal is to survive to share the footage and keep the focus on their misconduct, not to end up in a hospital bed. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Zines and DIY Media
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Zines and DIY Media] A friend asked me: 'Can selling zines actually help our budget?' What do I tell them?

Zines are the classic way to fund the fight while spreading the word. They're cheap to produce and people love to hold something real in their hands. If you put out a high-quality, punchy zine every quarter, you're creating a recurring revenue stream that also educates your base on the front lines.

title: Karl Organizing: Accountability
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Accountability] What if one group isn't doing the work they promised to do?

Have a direct, face-to-face conversation and ask them what the bottleneck is. If they are overwhelmed, offer help; if they are just being lazy or posturing, tell them they are holding back the whole movement. We don't have time for passengers when we're trying to sink the billionaire's ship, so everyone has to pull their weight or get out of the way. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Support] How do we find lawyers who will help us for free?

Let me break it down: Look for the National Lawyers Guild or local radical law collectives who prioritize movement work over big fat paychecks. Offer them office space or help with their own needs in exchange for 'Know Your Rights' trainings for the community. We need legal eagles who understand that the law is a tool for the powerful, but we can use it to shield our comrades. Never walk into a fight without knowing who you're going to call when the handcuffs come out.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, digital Security Practice
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, digital Security Practice] How do I keep my passwords safe without writing them down?

Use a password manager like Bitwarden or KeepassXC. Generate long, random strings for every site and use a master passphrase that you've memorized. Never reuse a password. If one site gets breached, you don't want the fascists having the keys to your entire life. Chip in to fund the fight for open-source tools that don't track us. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Security
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Security] Can you explain: can the police force me to unlock my phone during a protest?

Here's how it works: Disable your face-ID and thumbprint locks before you even leave the house; use a long passcode they can't just point at your face to bypass. If they demand your phone, tell them you do not consent to a search and stay silent. Your digital life is a map of our movement's networks, so protect it like you're guarding a comrade's life.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, safe Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, safe Zones] How do we make our neighborhood a 'no-go' zone for ICE?

Get local businesses to display stickers stating they won't let feds in without a warrant and train their staff on what to say. Map out every alley and 'safe house' where neighbors can duck in if they're being followed. Run regular drills so everyone knows exactly where to go when the alert hits. We create safety by making our neighborhoods too organized for the state to operate in. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Verification
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Verification] Can you explain: how do we avoid acting on fake reports of police activity?

Never share a report you haven't personally verified or heard from a trusted scout on the ground. Use a 'trusted source' protocol where two different people have to confirm the sighting before the alert goes out to the whole network. False alarms burn people out and make the network look unreliable. Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast when it comes to reporting state violence.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: legal Observers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: legal Observers] Give me the short version: Who are the people in the neon green hats and what do they do?

Those are Legal Observers, and they are our eyes and ears on the ground for the legal battle that follows the street fight. They aren't there to protest; they are there to document every badge number and every blow the pigs land. If you see an arrest, yell out the person's name so the observers can track them through the system.

title: Karl Organizing: Police Budgets
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Police Budgets] How do I talk about 'defunding' without losing the moderate vote?

Talk about 'investment' in the things that actually keep us safe: housing, healthcare, and youth programs. Point out that the police budget grows every year while the libraries close and the potholes stay empty. Ask your neighbors if they feel safer now than they did five years ago despite all that spending. We’re not just talking about taking money away; we’re talking about finally spending it on the people's actual needs. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Cop watch
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Cop watch] How do I start a cop watch program?

Get a team, get cameras, learn the law on filming police in your state. Patrol the areas where stops happen most. Film from a safe distance, announce you're recording, never interfere. Publish the footage — sunlight is the point. And train everyone on what to do if an officer turns on YOU.

title: Karl Organizing: Metadata Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Metadata Awareness] Can you explain: what is 'scrubbing' and how do I do it?

Scrubbing means stripping the hidden data—location, camera type, time—from your files. Use an app like 'ImagePipe' on Android or 'Metapho' on iOS before sharing any protest photos. For PDFs and docs, use the 'ExifTool' or simple online scrubbers. This prevents the state from using a 'cool photo' to pinpoint exactly where you stood at 2:00 PM.

title: Karl Organizing: Disability Accessibility
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Disability Accessibility] How do we make our mutual aid events more accessible for disabled comrades?

Start by asking disabled folks what they need instead of guessing and getting it wrong. Ensure every meeting spot has ramps and sensory-friendly spaces, and always provide captions or ASL if you're doing a presentation. Mutual aid that ignores the most marginalized among us isn't mutual—it's just a club for the able-bodied. Build accessibility into the foundation of your group so no one has to 'request' entry to their own community.

title: Karl Organizing: De-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[De-escalation] A friend asked me: 'How can we handle a neighborhood dispute without calling the cops?' What do I tell them?

Cops only bring guns to a conversation, so we handle our own business by sending a small team of neutral neighbors to listen to both sides. Focus on the harm done and how to fix it rather than who broke what rule. If things get heated, separate the parties and let tempers cool before trying to find a resolution. We build safety through relationships and accountability, not through handcuffs and cages. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Social pressure
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social pressure] How do we handle coworkers who are openly against the union?

Here's the thing: Don't waste all your energy on the hardcore 'no' votes. Focus on the 'undecideds' and the 'soft yes' folks. For the ones who are actively sabotaging, let their own friends and coworkers talk to them. Social pressure from peers is way more effective than any argument you can make. If they want to be the boss's pet, let them explain that to the people they work with every day.

title: Karl Organizing: Dispersal Orders
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dispersal Orders] What do we do when the cops give a dispersal order?

When the long-range acoustic device starts barking, you have to decide instantly: stay and risk the cage, or move to fight another day. If the group decides to hold the line, link arms and brace, but if the goal was a quick hit, move out immediately through your pre-planned exit routes. Never run—running triggers the cops' predatory instincts and leads to people getting trampled. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, labor Endorsements
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, labor Endorsements] How do I get unions to back a radical campaign?

Real talk: Show up on their picket lines long before you ask for their vote. Talk to the rank-and-file workers, not just the leadership, and prove you understand their specific grievances. Be the candidate who explicitly supports the right to strike and the expansion of collective bargaining. If you want the muscle of organized labor behind you, you have to be the most reliable ally they’ve ever seen in public office.

title: Karl Organizing: Sanctuary Spaces
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sanctuary Spaces] Can you explain: can we actually stop ICE from entering a house or church?

Here's the thing: Unless they have a judicial warrant signed by a judge with the specific address on it, they have no right to enter. Stand your ground at the door, record the interaction, and remind your neighbors not to open up or say a word. If they try to push through, make sure the whole neighborhood is outside with cameras rolling. Physical presence and public pressure are the best tools we have to keep families together.

title: Karl Organizing: The First Meeting
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The First Meeting] What is the most important thing to do at our very first coalition meeting?

Set a specific goal and a hard deadline for the first action before anyone leaves the room. Don't spend two hours introducing yourselves and sharing 'vibes'; identify the common enemy and decide on a date to make them sweat. A coalition that doesn't act immediately is just a book club with better slogans, and we are here to win, not study. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, childcare Collectives
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, childcare Collectives] How can we support the parents in our organizing circle who can't find sitters?

Look, Build a childcare rotation where those of us without kids take shifts watching the little ones during meetings and actions. It's not 'babysitting'; it's revolutionary support that allows parents—especially moms—to lead the fight. Make sure there's a safe, fun space with snacks and activities so the kids actually want to be there. We raise the next generation of rebels together, as a village, not as isolated nuclear families.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, eviction Defense] How do we stop a neighbor from being evicted?

When the sheriff shows up, you need a crowd of neighbors blocking the doors and the moving trucks. Organize a phone tree to flood the landlord's office with calls and let them know that an eviction will be more expensive and public than just letting the tenant stay. Move their furniture back in if they try to toss it. Housing is a right, and we defend it with our collective physical presence. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Rights Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Rights Training] Can you explain: what's the most important thing to teach neighbors about their rights?

The most powerful words anyone can say are 'I am remaining silent and I want a lawyer.' Teach everyone that the police are allowed to lie to you, so you should never believe a word they say during an interrogation. Run 'Know Your Rights' workshops in living rooms and parks until every kid on the block knows how to handle a stop. Knowledge is the first line of defense against the precinct.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, donor Capture] A wealthy businessman wants to give us a large sum but has some 'suggestions' on our messaging. Should we take it?

Tell him to keep his blood money and his opinions. The second you let a fat cat dictate your slogans is the second you stop being a threat to his class. If he wants to help, he can drop the cash in the bucket and walk away with no strings attached; otherwise, he's just buying a leash to put on your movement. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] A friend asked me: 'Is it safe to use my thumbprint to unlock my phone at a protest?' What do I tell them?

Absolutely not, comrade. The pigs can legally force your finger onto that sensor, but they can't easily force a complex passcode out of your brain. Disable all biometrics—FaceID and fingerprints—before you hit the streets. Switch to a six-digit PIN or a long passphrase. If you get snatched, that phone needs to be a digital brick they can't crack. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.
